text: https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.plsdof plsdof package provides Degrees Freedom estimates Partial Least Squares (PLS) Regression. Model selection PLS based various information criteria (aic, bic, gmdl) cross-validation. Estimates mean covariance PLS regression coefficients available. allow construction approximate confidence intervals application test procedures. , cross-validation procedures Ridge Regression Principal Components Regression available. plsdof package fully coded developped Nicole Kraemer Mikio L. Sugiyama (2012): “Degrees Freedom Partial Least Squares Regression”, Journal American Statistical Association, 106(494):697-705, doi:10.1198/jasa.2011.tm10107. title: Comparison of model selection criteria for Partial Least Squares Regression. — benchmark.pls
text: function estimates optimal number PLS components based four different criteria: (1) cross-validation, (2) information criteria naive Degrees Freedom DoF(m)=m+1, (3) information criteri Degrees Freedom computed via Lanczos represenation PLS (4) information criteri Degrees Freedom computed via Krylov represenation PLS. Note latter two options differ respect estimation model error. addition, function computes test error "zero model", .e. mean(y) training data used prediction. true.coefficients available, function also computes model error different methods, .e. sum squared differences true estimated regression coefficients.

title: Information criteria — information.criteria
text: Akaike information criterion (aic) defined $${aic}= \frac{{RSS}}{n} + 2\frac{{DoF}}{n} \sigma^ 2\,.$$ Bayesian information criterion (bic) defined $${bic}= \frac{{RSS}}{n} + log(n)\frac{{DoF}}{n} \sigma^ 2\,.$$ generalized minimum description length (gmdl) defined $$gmdl=\frac{n}{2}log(S)+\frac{DoF}{2}log(F)+\frac{1}{2}log(n)$$ $$S=\hat \sigma ^2$$ Note also possible use function information.criteria regression methods Partial Least Squares.

title: Model selection for Partial Least Squares based on information criteria — pls.ic

(2007) "Kernelizing PLS, Degrees Freedom, Efficient Model Selection", Proceedings 24th International Conference Machine Learning, Omni Press, 441 - 448 #' @examples # Boston Housing data data(Boston) X<-.matrix(Boston[,-14]) y<-.vector(Boston[,14]) # compute PLS coefficients first 5 components plot Degrees Freedom .pls1<-pls.model(X,y,m=5,compute.DoF=TRUE) plot(0:5,.pls1$DoF,pch="*",cex=3,xlab="components",ylab="DoF",ylim=c(0,14)) # add naive estimate lines(0:5,1:6,lwd=3) # model selection Bayesian Information criterion mypls2<-pls.ic(X,y,criterion="bic") # model selection based cross-validation. # returns estimated covariance matrix regression coefficients mypls3<-pls.cv(X,y,compute.covariance=TRUE) .vcov<-vcov(mypls3) .sd<-sqrt(diag(.vcov)) # standard deviation regression coefficients
